before.descent_text: This is a walk-off/downclimb — there is no rappelling on this route. From the summit, reverse the exposed Class 3 south-ridge scramble down to the top of the south snowfield, then descend the snowfield back onto the Whatcom Glacier at roughly 5,200-5,500 ft. Rope back up for glacier travel and reverse the traverse across the east/south side of the peak toward Perfect Pass and back to Whatcom Pass; crevasses and moats are typically more open on the descent as the afternoon sun softens the snowpack, so budget time for careful navigation rather than a quick glissade — the glacier can deteriorate to bare ice with gaping moats later in the season. From Whatcom Pass, descend the same trail system used on approach: the climbers' path down to Graybeal Camp, the Brush Creek/Chilliwack River Trail back to the cable-car crossing of the Chilliwack River, then back up and over Hannegan Pass and down the Hannegan Pass Trail to the trailhead. Given the roughly 17+ trail miles one-way just to reach Whatcom Pass, most parties camp at Graybeal, Whatcom Camp, or near Perfect Pass and treat this as a multi-day trip rather than a car-to-car push, descending only as far as the next camp on summit day. If the summit notch is badly melted out and choss-prone, an alternate descent drops about 200 ft north of Peak 7347 to reach the Wiley Glacier instead of reversing through the notch.

itinerary.cal: Overnight camps (Easy Saddle, Perfect Pass, US Cabin Camp) require a North Cascades NP wilderness permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center; best conditions on the south-face snowfield are typically July-August before it thins out.

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day/3-night loop via Easy Ridge in and Whatcom Pass out — essentially the same approach as the Southwest Route, but the summit day climbs the exposed Class 3 south ridge crest directly rather than traversing the glacier. Roughly 37-39 mi round trip with over 10,000 ft of cumulative gain.

before.descent_text: This is a non-technical walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling involved. From the summit (7,574 ft), reverse the south ridge crest — an exposed but straightforward Class 3 scramble — down to the top of the south-facing snowfield, then descend the snowfield (glissade-able in the right conditions, early-mid season) back to Perfect Pass. From Perfect Pass, most parties simply reverse the Easy Ridge approach (down through the Impasse workaround to Easy Saddle, then out via Hannegan Pass). Parties doing a Picket-range traverse or looping back toward Whatcom Pass instead descend via the low-orbit traverse around the peak's east side, or cross the Whatcom Glacier directly when it is 'in' and consolidated (rope up for glacier travel and watch for moats near the pass) — parties describe this glacier crossing as straightforward in good late-summer conditions but it should not be treated as guaranteed snow-covered/moat-free. No fixed anchors or rappel stations exist on this route; rappels = 0.

before.rope_note: 4th-class variation on the same peak as the North Ridge; typically unroped scrambling with exposure, occasionally protected with a short handline on steeper steps.
before.approach: The standard approach begins at the Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of Hannegan Pass Rd/FS-32 off SR 542, ~3,100 ft), following Hannegan Pass Trail #674 about 4 miles and 2,000 ft of gain to Hannegan Pass (~5,050-5,100 ft). From the pass, the trail switchbacks down the far side into the Chilliwack River valley to Boundary Camp, then continues down-valley to the Chilliwack River crossing — a ford that can be thigh-deep and swift at mid-summer flow and is the approach's main hazard; check levels before committing, and expect it to be harder earlier in the season or after rain. From the ford, leave the maintained trail system and pick up the old, unmaintained Easy Ridge climbers' trail, which climbs steeply out of the valley to Easy Saddle (~5,200 ft, a common camp, roughly 5.5-8.5 hours/8-9 miles from the trailhead depending on pace and the ford). From Easy Saddle the route follows the crest of Easy Ridge, over or around Easy Peak (6,613 ft, ascend its south ridge), to the notorious 'Imperfect Impasse' — a notch guarded by deep snow moats on both sides and down-sloping, often-wet slabs. In many seasons the direct crossing is unsafe or impassable; the established workaround drops roughly 800 ft down to about 4,400 ft and re-climbs a exposed Class 4 rock step (many parties belay this) to regain the ridge on the far side. Beyond the Impasse the trail continues to Perfect Pass (~6,200 ft), the standard high camp for Whatcom Peak, about 8-9 hours/12-13 miles in from the trailhead for a strong party. There is no reliable water at Perfect Pass itself in late season — plan to fill up at Easy Saddle or from snowmelt. An alternative approach skips Easy Ridge entirely: from Whatcom Pass (reached via the Chilliwack River/Brush Creek trail or the Little Beaver Creek Trail from Ross Lake — see the North Ridge route for that approach), a 'low orbit' traverse around Whatcom Peak's east side on scree and snow reaches the same south-side snowfields without crossing the Impasse, but it exposes climbers to the moats and possible crevasses at the edge of the Whatcom Glacier and should be treated as glacier travel (rope/crevasse-rescue gear) in early season.

approach_variants.name: Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack ford and Easy Ridge over the Imperfect Impasse to Perfect Pass
approach_variants.notes:
From the Hannegan Pass Trailhead at the end of Hannegan Pass Road, FS-32, off SR-542 at about 3,100 ft, Trail #674 runs about 4 miles and 2,000 ft to Hannegan Pass at roughly 5,050-5,100 ft. The trail then switchbacks down the far side into the Chilliwack River valley to Boundary Camp and continues down-valley to the Chilliwack River crossing.

That ford is the approach's main hazard: it can be thigh-deep and swift at mid-summer flow, and is harder earlier in the season or after rain. From the ford, leave the maintained trail system and pick up the old, unmaintained Easy Ridge climbers' trail, which climbs steeply out of the valley to Easy Saddle at about 5,200 ft, a common camp, roughly 5.5 to 8.5 hours and 8-9 miles in depending on pace and the ford.

From Easy Saddle the route follows the crest over or around Easy Peak at 6,613 ft to the Imperfect Impasse, then continues to Perfect Pass at about 6,200 ft, the standard high camp, about 8-9 hours and 12-13 miles in for a strong party. There is no reliable water at Perfect Pass in late season; fill at Easy Saddle or from snowmelt.
hazards: A thigh-deep, swift ford of the Chilliwack River at mid-summer flow
The Imperfect Impasse: snow moats, wet down-sloping slabs, and an 800 ft descent to an exposed class 4 step as the workaround
Moats where the south snowfield meets the summit rock, worse late season
A short but very exposed summit crest on poor rock with limited protection
No reliable water at Perfect Pass in late season
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE ROUTE STARTS WHERE THE CAMP ENDS: FROM PERFECT PASS, HEAD NORTH AND UP ONTO THE BROAD SOUTH SNOWFIELD. That snowfield is the lower margin of the Whatcom Glacier, the angle is moderate, and the line aims at a CONSPICUOUS COL IN THE SUMMIT RIDGE above. Reports describe it as long but straightforward, roughly an hour from the pass.

SO THE AIMING POINT IS A NOTCH IN A SKYLINE, AND IN CLOUD THE SUBSTITUTE FOR IT IS THIS: keep climbing snow at a moderate angle until the snow RUNS OUT AGAINST ROCK. The snowfield is left at the col. Where snow meets rock is where a moat or a lip of hard snow is most likely to be awkward, and it is worse late in the season, which is exactly why you will notice it.

CONFIRM ABOVE: the final stretch along the crest is SHORT, on the order of a hundred feet, but very exposed with drops on both sides, on poor rock with limited protection. Many parties belay it even though the moves are only third to fourth class. If you are on a long ridge rather than a hundred-foot one, you are not on this route.

THE VARIATION THAT IS NOT AN ERROR: some parties break out onto ramps and ledges to the NORTHEAST of the col and rejoin the crest higher. Both reach the same place.

THE IMPASSE, WHICH IS THE OTHER THING YOU HAVE TO FIND ON THIS APPROACH: it is a notch guarded by deep snow moats on both sides and down-sloping, often wet slabs. In many seasons the direct crossing is unsafe or impassable; the established workaround drops roughly 800 ft to about 4,400 ft and re-climbs an exposed class 4 rock step, which many parties belay, to regain the ridge on the far side. Dropping 800 ft to get past a notch feels wrong and is correct.

approach_variants.name: The low-orbit traverse from Whatcom Pass, skipping Easy Ridge and the Impasse entirely
approach_variants.notes: An alternative that avoids the Impasse. From Whatcom Pass, reached via the Chilliwack River and Brush Creek trails or via the Little Beaver Creek Trail from Ross Lake, a low-orbit traverse around Whatcom Peak's east side on scree and snow reaches the same south-side snowfields.
approach_variants.season: Jul-Sep; treat as glacier travel in early season
hazards: Moats and possible crevasses at the edge of the Whatcom Glacier; treat as glacier travel in early season
Scree and snow sidehilling with no path
The same summit crest exposure as the Easy Ridge variant
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THIS VARIANT IS DEFINED BY WHAT IT AVOIDS, AND THAT IS THE TEST: IF YOU HAVE CROSSED THE IMPASSE, YOU ARE NOT ON IT. The low orbit contours around the peak's east side instead of over the ridge crest, and delivers you onto the same south-side snowfields the Easy Ridge line reaches from Perfect Pass.

ARRIVAL IS THE SAME ARRIVAL: broad moderate snow below a conspicuous col in the summit ridge, and the route is where the snow runs out against rock.

WHAT YOU TRADE FOR IT, AND WHY THE CHOICE IS A CONDITIONS CALL RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: the low orbit exposes you to the moats and possible crevasses at the edge of the WHATCOM GLACIER, so it should be treated as glacier travel with a rope and crevasse-rescue gear in early season. The Impasse is a rock problem; this is a glacier problem. Pick the one your party is equipped for.
